source_text:
Ἡ δὲ εἰς ἡμᾶς φθάσασα ἱστορία, ὑπό τινων μὲν λεγόντων, ὅτι

Κλήμης ὁ γενόμενος ἐπίσκοπος Ῥωμαίων ἔγραψε Ἐπιστολήν· ὑπό τινων δὲ, ὅτι
Λουκᾶς ὁ γράψας τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ τὰς Πράξεις.
thought_title: The tradition that reached us about the epistle's writer
orientation: Origen is closing his discussion of Hebrews' authorship by reporting the two traditions that have reached him about who wrote it.
pass_a_gloss: But the tradition that reached us, some saying that Clement, who became bishop of the Romans, wrote the Epistle; but others, that Luke, who wrote the Gospel and the Acts, did.

choices.term: ἡ δὲ εἰς ἡμᾶς φθάσασα ἱστορία
choices.english: But the tradition that reached us
choices.why: Keeps the adversative δέ and renders ἱστορία with the glossary's 'tradition'; φθάσασα as 'reached' preserves the perfective sense of arrival.
rejected: But the account that came to us
But the history that arrived to us

choices.why: Renders the genitive absolute with μὲν as a participial clause, preserving the contrast with the following δέ.
rejected: on the one hand by some saying

choices.english: Clement, who became bishop of the Romans
choices.why: Uses the brief's name 'Clement of Rome' in the gloss while keeping the source's participial phrase 'who became bishop of the Romans' literally.
rejected: Clement who was made bishop of Rome
Clement, the one who became bishop of the Romans

choices.term: Λουκᾶς ὁ γράψας τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ τὰς Πράξεις
choices.english: Luke, who wrote the Gospel and the Acts
choices.why: Keeps the articular participle 'who wrote' and the definite articles on Gospel and Acts, matching the source's identification of Luke.
rejected: Luke the writer of the Gospel and Acts
Luke, the one who wrote the Gospel and the Acts

pass_b_english: The tradition that has come down to us says that some claim Clement of Rome, who became bishop of the Romans, wrote the Epistle, while others claim it was Luke, the one who wrote the Gospel and Acts.

last_rejected.source_quote: Λουκᾶς ὁ γράψας τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον, καὶ τὰς Πράξεις
last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'wrote' for Luke's source form; brief maps to modern name.
last_rejected.fix: Luke, the author of the Gospel and Acts
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ γράψας is correctly rendered 'the one who wrote'; no glossary issue evident.

last_rejected.quote: The tradition that has come down to us says that some claim
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἡ δὲ εἰς ἡμᾶς φθάσασα ἱστορία, ὑπό τινων μὲν λεγόντων
last_rejected.why: Source: tradition from some saying; English adds extra 'says that' layer.
last_rejected.fix: The tradition that has come down to us from some says that Clement...
last_rejected.ruling: ἱστορία + λεγόντων naturally yields 'tradition...says that some claim'; no meaning change.

problems.fix: Standardize to 'Luke, author of Gospel and Acts'
